workload.py.text:
"""Self-expiring workload fixture; process ownership is implemented only by Java."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time


def report(destination):
    membership = Path('/proc/self/cgroup').read_text().strip()
    pending = Path(destination).with_suffix('.pending')
    pending.write_text(
        f'pid={os.getpid()}\nuid={os.getuid()}\ngid={os.getgid()}\n'
        f'groups={os.getgroups()}\npgid={os.getpgrp()}\n'
        f'cgroup={membership}\ntoken={os.environ.get("OWNER_GATE_TOKEN", "missing")}\n')
    os.replace(pending, destination)


if sys.argv[1] == 'leaf':
    report(sys.argv[2])
    time.sleep(20)
else:
    report(sys.argv[2])
    subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, __file__, 'leaf', sys.argv[3]],
                     start_new_session=True, close_fds=True)
    os._exit(7)

limitations: The supervisor must be a dedicated elevated JVM with no unrelated children. Shared-JVM waitpid/reaper coordination is unaccepted.

This candidate uses Linux cgroup v2 management authority already established by accepted evidence, and explicit unprivileged UID/GID1001 for the native gates. It is not an unprivileged delegation implementation or a hostile-workload escape proof.

The demonstrated completion path is terminate followed by root/adopted reaping. Natural completion without terminate/close needs an explicit observe-and-reap operation before production integration: adoptedDrained is currently set by stopAndReap only.
The gate uses fixed short readiness/root/reaping deadlines appropriate to tiny fixtures. Production cancellation/time limits and long-build waiting require scheduler integration.
The controlled failure is after successful prepare and before release. Exhaustive syscall failure injection and shared-JVM integration remain untested.
macOS/Windows process-owner composition and production scheduler integration are unaccepted. No Codex build was run.
